guides.keywords: electrical system restoration pixel repair, window regulators, lighting, and module faults. the usual e46 electrical problems and their fixes. intermediate restoration address as symptoms appear $400-1,000 torx driver set (t10, t15, t20, t25) small flathead screwdriver trim panel removal tools (plastic pry set) soldering iron with fine tip solder and flux heat gun or hair dryer multimeter wire strippers and crimpers electrical contact cleaner dielectric grease inpa/ista diagnostic software (optional) start with instrument cluster pixel repair—remove cluster (4 torx screws, disconnect cables). disassemble cluster housing to access the lcd display ribbon cable. use heat gun to warm existing ribbon, carefully peel off failed ribbon. e46 pixel failure is extremely common—repair is straightforward with the right ribbon. window regulator cables fray before breaking—listen for unusual sounds during operation.

guides.title: Interior Restoration
guides.description: Leather, headliner, trim, and climate control. The door card and headliner fabric are the first things to go.
guides.keywords: interior restoration leather, headliner, trim, and climate control. the door card and headliner fabric are the first things to go. intermediate restoration as needed for wear items $300-800 trim panel removal tools (plastic) torx driver set (t15, t20, t25, t30) phillips and flathead screwdrivers heat gun adhesive spreader or brush masking tape and paper microfiber cloths leather cleaner and conditioner interior detailing brushes spray bottle razor blade (new, for trim removal) sunroof drain snake/compressed air begin with thorough interior cleaning—vacuum all surfaces and crevices. clean leather with dedicated leather cleaner, working in small sections. address leather cracks with repair compound—clean, fill, texture, and color match. e46 leather tends to crack on the driver's bolster—address early to prevent spreading. headliner sag is caused by foam deterioration—full replacement is the only permanent fix.

guides.title: Rear Subframe Mount Inspection
guides.description: Before you buy an E46, or before you add power or track time to one, check the rear subframe mounting points. Cracks there are the most expensive E46 problem, and this is how to spot them early.
guides.keywords: rear subframe mount inspection before you buy an e46, or before you add power or track time to one, check the rear subframe mounting points. cracks there are the most expensive e46 problem, and this is how to spot them early. intermediate restoration  $0-50 jack stands or a lift bright flashlight and inspection mirror borescope camera (inexpensive usb type works) screwdriver for trim wire brush raise the rear of the car securely on stands or a lift. remove the rear wheels for better access to the mounting points. clean around the four subframe mounting points where they meet the body. reinforcement kits (plates welded to the floor) are the long-term fix, and should be done by a competent welder. worn subframe bushings can mimic a cracked floor. check both.

guides.title: Oil Change
guides.description: Oil and filter on the M54.
guides.keywords: oil change oil and filter on the m54. easy diy every 7,500 miles or annually $50-70 17mm socket for drain plug 36mm socket or oil filter wrench drain pan funnel torque wrench jack and jack stands warm the engine for 2-3 minutes to thin the oil for better drainage. raise the front of the car safely and support on jack stands. position drain pan under the oil pan and remove the 17mm drain plug. the e46 uses a cartridge-style filter—the housing stays in place. always replace the o-ring to prevent leaks from the filter housing.

guides.title: Expansion Tank Replacement
guides.description: Replace the plastic expansion tank before it cracks and leaves you stranded.
guides.keywords: expansion tank replacement replace the plastic expansion tank before it cracks and leaves you stranded. easy diy every 60,000 miles (preventive) $40-70 10mm socket flathead screwdriver pliers for hose clamps drain pan new coolant (1 gallon bmw blue) allow the engine to cool completely—never open a hot cooling system. remove the expansion tank cap slowly to release any residual pressure. place drain pan under the expansion tank area. inspect the old tank carefully—cracks often start at the seams or sensor fitting. this is a known failure point—replace preventively rather than waiting for failure.

guides.title: Brake Pad Replacement
guides.description: Front and rear pads, including resetting the pad wear sensor.
guides.keywords: brake pad replacement front and rear pads, including resetting the pad wear sensor. easy diy every 25,000-50,000 miles $60-120 17mm socket for lug bolts 7mm allen socket for caliper pins flathead screwdriver brake caliper piston tool or c-clamp wire brush brake cleaner brake grease jack and jack stands loosen lug bolts slightly while the car is on the ground. raise and support the car safely on jack stands. remove wheel and set aside. always replace pads in axle pairs—never replace just one side. e46 wear sensors are on front left and rear right—reset the cbs if equipped.

guides.title: Cooling System Refresh
guides.description: Water pump, thermostat, and hoses in one go. The E46 cooling system is the most common way these cars leave people on the shoulder.
guides.keywords: cooling system refresh water pump, thermostat, and hoses in one go. the e46 cooling system is the most common way these cars leave people on the shoulder. intermediate diy every 60,000-80,000 miles $300-500 32mm wrench for fan clutch fan clutch holding tool 10mm, 13mm sockets e10 torx socket flathead screwdriver drain pan pliers for hose clamps new coolant (1.5 gallons) spill-free funnel ensure engine is completely cool before starting. remove the intake snorkel and cabin filter housing cover for access. remove the fan clutch using 32mm wrench and holding tool (left-hand thread—clockwise to loosen). the fan clutch is left-hand threaded—turn clockwise to remove, counter-clockwise to tighten. use a water pump with metal impeller—plastic impellers can fail catastrophically.

guides.title: Complete Suspension Refresh
guides.description: Control arms, thrust arms, and the rear trailing arm bushings. At this age, most E90s are due.
guides.keywords: complete suspension refresh control arms, thrust arms, and the rear trailing arm bushings. at this age, most e90s are due. intermediate restoration every 80,000-100,000 miles $600-1,200 floor jack and jack stands (4) 18mm, 19mm, 21mm sockets and wrenches ball joint separator tie rod end puller breaker bar torque wrench (ft-lb range) penetrating oil rtab press tool or hydraulic press spring compressor alignment specs printout raise vehicle and support on jack stands at all four corners. remove all wheels and photograph suspension for reference. soak all suspension bolts with penetrating oil before removal. e90 rtabs make a big difference to rear-end stability—prioritize if worn. the e90 uses similar suspension to e46 but with updated components.

guides.title: Rust Prevention and Inspection
guides.description: A well-protected chassis, but not a perfect one. Where to look and how to keep it clean underneath.
guides.keywords: rust prevention and inspection a well-protected chassis, but not a perfect one. where to look and how to keep it clean underneath. intermediate restoration inspect annually $100-1,500+ inspection mirror and flashlight wire brush and wire wheel angle grinder with flap disc mig welder (if repairs needed) sandpaper (80-320 grit) primer and paint supplies safety glasses and respirator fire extinguisher spray wand for cavity wax e90s are well-protected but still require inspection, especially salt-belt cars. clean undercarriage thoroughly before inspection. inspect rocker panels by tapping with screwdriver—soft spots indicate rust. e90s are generally more rust-resistant than earlier bmws due to better galvanization. most rust issues are from stone chips, salt, and debris rather than design flaws.

guides.title: Electrical System Service
guides.description: Ignition coils, VANOS solenoids, battery registration, and coding. Replace a battery on an E90 without registering it and you'll shorten its life.
guides.keywords: electrical system service ignition coils, vanos solenoids, battery registration, and coding. replace a battery on an e90 without registering it and you'll shorten its life. intermediate restoration address as symptoms appear $300-800 ista/inpa diagnostic software or compatible tool torx driver set (t20, t25, t30) 10mm socket spark plug socket trim removal tools multimeter battery registration tool soldering iron (for module repair) contact cleaner dielectric grease disconnect battery and wait 10 minutes before electrical work. start with diagnostic scan—e90s require proper software for full diagnosis. for ignition coil replacement: remove engine cover, disconnect coil connectors. e90 requires proper diagnostic software—generic obd2 scanners miss many faults. battery must be registered after replacement or it will overcharge and fail early.

guides.title: Interior Restoration
guides.description: Leather, trim, iDrive, and the common wear items.
guides.keywords: interior restoration leather, trim, idrive, and the common wear items. intermediate restoration as needed for wear items $250-900 trim removal tools (plastic pry set) torx driver set (t15, t20, t25, t30) phillips and flathead screwdrivers heat gun adhesive scraper microfiber cloths leather cleaner and conditioner interior detailing brushes ista diagnostic for idrive coding document all components with photos before disassembly. remove seats for access - 4 bolts each, disconnect electrical connectors. for leather: clean with dedicated leather cleaner in small sections. e90 aluminum trim peels and flakes—vinyl wrap is popular solution. sport seats have aggressive bolsters that wear faster.

guides.title: Electric Water Pump and Thermostat (N52/N54/N55)
guides.description: The E90's electric water pump fails without warning, and the dash goes straight to limp mode. Do the pump and thermostat together, before it strands you.
guides.keywords: electric water pump and thermostat (n52/n54/n55) the e90's electric water pump fails without warning, and the dash goes straight to limp mode. do the pump and thermostat together, before it strands you. intermediate restoration  $400-800 jack stands torx and e-torx sockets 10mm, 13mm sockets drain pan battery charger (for the bleeding procedure) let the engine cool completely, then raise the front of the car. remove the under-engine splash shield and drain the coolant. remove the air intake components for access to the front of the engine. use genuine or original-supplier pumps. cheap pumps are why some cars are on their third. a pump that's making noise or throwing a code is nearly done.

guides.title: Oil Change
guides.description: Oil and filter on the N52, N54, and N55.
guides.keywords: oil change oil and filter on the n52, n54, and n55. easy diy every 7,500-10,000 miles $60-90 17mm socket for drain plug 36mm socket or oil filter cap wrench drain pan funnel jack and jack stands torque wrench warm the engine for 2-3 minutes to thin the oil. raise the front of the car and secure on jack stands, or use ramps. locate the oil drain plug on the oil pan—passenger side. the e90 uses a cartridge filter—the housing stays on the engine. always replace the o-ring to prevent leaks from the filter housing cap.

guides.title: Brake Pad Replacement
guides.description: Front and rear pads, including resetting the electronic wear sensor and the service interval.
guides.keywords: brake pad replacement front and rear pads, including resetting the electronic wear sensor and the service interval. easy diy every 25,000-50,000 miles $80-150 17mm socket for lug bolts 7mm allen socket for caliper pins t30 torx for wear sensor brake piston tool or c-clamp wire brush brake cleaner brake grease diagnostic tool for cbs reset (optional) loosen lug bolts while the car is on the ground. raise and support the car on jack stands, remove wheel. disconnect the brake pad wear sensor connector and unclip from bracket. e90 electronic wear sensors are usually on front left and rear right. after replacement, reset the cbs (condition based service) brake indicator.

guides.title: Spark Plug Replacement
guides.description: Plugs on every E90 engine. The turbo engines want them more often than you'd think, so check the interval.
guides.keywords: spark plug replacement plugs on every e90 engine. the turbo engines want them more often than you'd think, so check the interval. easy diy every 60,000 miles (n52) or 45,000 miles (n54/n55) $60-120 10mm socket t30 torx spark plug socket (5/8" or 14mm thin-wall) 6" extension torque wrench compressed air or vacuum anti-seize (optional—some plugs pre-applied) allow engine to cool completely—spark plugs can seize in hot aluminum. remove the engine cover by pulling up on the four corners. disconnect the electrical connector from each ignition coil. n54 uses 6 spark plugs; the n52 uses 6 spark plugs—one per cylinder. use ngk or bosch oem-equivalent plugs for best results.

guides.title: Oil Filter Housing Gasket
guides.description: The oil filter housing gasket leaks on almost every N52/N54/N55 eventually. Fix it before the oil finds the belts.
guides.keywords: oil filter housing gasket the oil filter housing gasket leaks on almost every n52/n54/n55 eventually. fix it before the oil finds the belts. intermediate diy as needed (common leak point) $30-60 36mm socket for filter cap e10, e12 torx sockets 10mm socket flathead screwdriver gasket pick clean rags new gasket kit fresh oil for top-off remove the engine cover and intake snorkel for access. drain some coolant—the oil cooler (if equipped) ties into the cooling system. remove the oil filter cap and filter element. the ofhg is one of the most common oil leaks on n52 and n54 engines. oil dripping onto the exhaust can cause smoke and fire—don't delay this repair.
